source.branch: When a hero who cannot reach the floor drops an ordinary touchstone on the stairs while levitating, do.c:drop checks finesse_ahriman, prints the verbose drop message, frees the inventory object, and calls hitfloor(obj, TRUE). On ordinary non-soft, non-altar terrain, hitfloor prints the hit-surface message, tests hero_breaks and ship_object in that order, then places a surviving object with dropz. Other surface, trap, altar, breakage and shipping branches are part of the whole function.
callers: do.c:drop lines 758-773 calls dothrow.c:hitfloor when !can_reach_floor(TRUE); js/do.js:drop currently throws before the object removal and hitfloor call.
dothrow.c:throwit, invent.c:hold_another_object, and other C callers also reach hitfloor; audit the production JavaScript callers when wiring the complete function.
dependencies: artifact.c:finesse_ahriman returns the levitation artifact special case consumed by do.c:drop; the JavaScript helper exists.
dothrow.c:hero_breaks returns a Boolean; dokick.c:ship_object returns a Boolean; preserve their source order and current caller environments.
do.c:dropz is the final floor placement path and may reach flooreffects, shop, and redraw operations; the caller must pass the operations needed by the actual state without a case-specific whitelist.
Altar surfaces call do.c:doaltarobj, and a levitation artifact can call trap.c:float_down after hitfloor; preserve these source-ordered branches or record only discarded void gaps.
